title: Landing page
notes: One file carrying en, ru and uk in-page; its hreflang cluster also names the ten per-language landings.

title: App privacy policy
notes: The 'What it accesses and why' and 'Local files it writes' blocks are rendered from docs/security-posture.json by scripts/security-posture.ps1 -Render; the rest of the page is authored.

title: Install trust page
notes: The INSTALL-TRUST contract page; its 'What the app never does' section must say what privacy.html says.

title: Extension privacy policy
notes: The URL both extension stores are given. The 'Network access' and 'Permissions' blocks are rendered from docs/security-posture.json; the rest is authored.

title: Per-language landing pages
notes: Machine-translated, one language per page, self-canonical. Listed by path rather than by glob, so a new language folder reaches the sitemap only through this record.

title: Sitemap
notes: Rendered by scripts/doc-registry.ps1 -Generate from the records above that announce pages; never edited by hand.

title: Robots file
notes: Names the sitemap by its absolute address, which is where the registry tools read the site's base URL.

title: Repository README trio
notes: Published as the GitHub repository's front page, not on the Pages site.

title: Microsoft Store listing sources
notes: Thirteen locales, rendered into the Partner Center CSV by tools/store/build-store-listing-csv.ps1 and served by the Microsoft Store.

title: Partner Center listing CSV
notes: Render target patched by tools/store/build-store-listing-csv.ps1 from the listing sources; never hand-edited.

title: Extension store listing and store privacy text
notes: The texts pasted into the Chrome Web Store and Edge Add-ons forms. The permission justifications in LISTING.md and the network and permission sections of PRIVACY.md are rendered from docs/security-posture.json; the rest is authored.

title: Licence and third-party notices
notes: Shipped inside the distributed packages and the extension; not site pages.

title: Security posture inventories
notes: The permission and network-surface inventories of canon SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY section 7, and the source every public privacy form renders from. An engineering record for whoever changes what the product can touch or send, so it is not announced.

title: Security posture, readable form
notes: Rendered by scripts/security-posture.ps1 -Render from docs/security-posture.json for reading in the repository; never edited by hand.

title: Documentation registry
notes: This registry and its coverage exclusions (canon DOCUMENTATION_CONCEPT section 6); checked by scripts/doc-registry.ps1, queried by scripts/doc-query.ps1. Tooling input, not something a reader lands on.

title: docs/ index
notes: The table of the public-facing engineering documents; repository reading, not a site page.

title: Cross-edition parity contract
notes: The Go to JS port map, the invariants both editions hold and the intentional divergences; read before any user-facing feature.

title: Glyph map
notes: Every glyph each surface draws, mapped to the shared icon vocabulary; read before changing an icon.

title: Spec lifecycle method
notes: The tooling-agnostic method behind the spec commands; repository reading for contributors.

title: winget submission walkthrough
notes: A dated walkthrough of the winget submission with its blockers; a maintainer's reference, not user documentation.

title: Shared contract pointers
notes: One pointer per shared contract this product produces or consumes (REPO-LAYOUT rule 2); the contracts themselves live in the catalog named in AGENTS.md.

title: Agent rules
notes: The repository's operating instructions for coding agents (REPO-LAYOUT rule 1); AGENTS.md is authoritative.

title: Agent commands and subagents
notes: The slash commands and subagent definitions the agent runtime loads; tooling, not reading material.

title: Developer notes
notes: Developer-oriented notes on local builds and the CLI; repository reading.

title: Release flow and publish state
notes: The build-versus-release definition and the per-channel publish state; maintainer reading.

title: Engineering ledger
notes: Ledger shape 2, the stamp's ledgerFile. Its release entries feed the store and GitHub notes; the ledger itself is repository reading.

title: Local build commit log
notes: Appended by scripts/build-local.ps1 on every local build commit; never edited by hand.

title: Ship-together surfaces manifest
notes: The list of user-facing surfaces that move together when a feature ships, driven by the docs-sync command.

title: Open tickets and the release queue
notes: Public collaborative specifications, their tactical plans and RELEASE_QUEUE.md; working documents for contributors, not user reading.

title: Finished tickets
notes: Frozen archive (REPO-LAYOUT rule 6): a finished ticket keeps its name and text; only a move into it changes it.

title: Research notes

sitemap_exclude.reason: A test page built for the page-OCR placement measurement and loaded by a headless browser; an instrument of that note, not a page for readers.

notes: Measured findings kept for the tickets that cite them. New notes are named RESEARCH_<topic-slug>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md, as CLAUDE.md declares; the lowercase names predate that and stay, because tickets and the frozen archive link to them.

title: Research and quality method references
notes: Methodology the agent rules link to (CLAUDE.md); they sit beside the research notes but are not findings.

title: Early-project notes
notes: Frozen planning notes from March to June 2026, superseded by DEV/plan/, AGENTS.md and the canon; kept as history and never updated.

title: Extension README and publishing notes
notes: The extension edition's developer and publishing reference; repository reading.

title: MSIX packaging notes
notes: How the Store package is built and uploaded; maintainer reading.

title: OCR fidelity lab README
notes: The OCR visual-fidelity lab's usage and contributor rules; developer tooling reference.

title: Shared appearance description
notes: Explains appearance.json, the one description of the OCR overlay and reader palette both editions derive from; developer reference.
